title: Lesson 8: The X-Factor — Urdhva Criss-Cross Multiplication
learningGoals: Identify the three steps of the Urdhva-Tiryak pattern visually.
Multiply any 2-digit × 2-digit number using criss-cross without a calculator.
Handle carry digits correctly in each of the three steps.
coreIdeas: Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam means vertically and crosswise — three partial products placed in order.
Step 1 (right): units × units. Step 2 (middle): cross multiply then add. Step 3 (left): tens × tens.
Carry from each step is added to the next step's partial product — just like normal addition.

workedExamples.method: Step1: 3×4=12, write 2 carry 1. Step2: 2×4+3×1+1=12, write 2 carry 1. Step3: 2×1+1=3. Answer: 322.
Step1: 7×6=42, write 2 carry 4. Step2: 4×6+7×3+4=55, write 5 carry 5. Step3: 4×3+5=17. Answer: 1692.

starterPractice: Draw two 2-digit numbers and label their tens and units digits.
What is 3 × 4? What is 2 × 4 + 3 × 1? (Practise the cross step.)
23 × 11 — can you use the simpler ×11 trick first, then verify with criss-cross?

onboarding.coachIntro: Hi! I am Arya, your Vedic Maths coach. Today you will learn the most powerful multiplication trick in Vedic Maths — the criss-cross or X pattern. After this, you will multiply ANY two 2-digit numbers in your head!
onboarding.placementRule: Start at group A. If the learner already knows steps 1 and 2, start at group E.

mission.missionPromise: Master the 3-step Urdhva pattern and multiply any 2-digit numbers in under 10 seconds.
mission.successCelebration: X-Factor champion! You can now multiply any 2-digit × 2-digit number using the ancient Vedic pattern. Incredible!

microLessonPattern: Coach draws the X arrows over the two numbers on the board.
Step-by-step board reveals each partial product in order.
Student traces the X arrows with their finger before answering.
Student computes one step at a time before seeing the full answer.
Instant feedback points to the exact step that was wrong.
Review asks student to say the 3 steps in their own words.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 18 XP per exercise group based on difficulty.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak counter visible; a correct answer on retry still counts as streak-save.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each group earns a themed badge tied to the criss-cross skill.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short coach cheer, XP pulse animation, and progress bar moves forward.

reviewLoop.trigger: Two wrong answers in one group triggers a mini re-teach showing the X diagram again.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Re-draw the criss-cross arrows, then give a simpler multiplication.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the student answers the checkpoint correctly.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Missed groups reappear at the start of the next session as warm-up cards.

uiDirectives.noScrollGoal: Student sees mission progress, question card, and action buttons without scrolling.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Imagine drawing an X between two 2-digit numbers. The three lines of the X give you three partial products — right vertical, two diagonals, left vertical!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: For 23 × 14: Step1 (right) = 3×4=12. Step2 (cross) = 2×4+3×1. Step3 (left) = 2×1. Show X lines in colour.
sessionFlow.readAloudPrompt: Name the three steps of the criss-cross.
sessionFlow.tryPrompt: For 21 × 32, what is the RIGHT vertical step?
sessionFlow.masteryCheck: What is the middle (cross) step for 21 × 32?
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Excellent! You identified the X pattern — now let us compute each step.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Draw the X arrows for 31 × 22 and label each step.

exercises.questionText: In the criss-cross method, Step 1 (right vertical) of 23 × 14 gives:
exercises.hint: Step 1 is the units digits only: units of first × units of second.

exercises.questionText: In criss-cross 21 × 32, the MIDDLE (cross) step is:
exercises.hint: Cross: tens of first × units of second + units of first × tens of second.

sessionFlow.coachHook: Let us master Step 1 first. Multiply the two UNITS digits. Write the units digit of the result, carry the tens.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Step 1 locked in — units column done!

exercises.questionText: Step 1 (units × units) of 34 × 21: units digit written and carry?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Step 2 is the X — two diagonal multiplications added together, plus any carry from Step 1.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect cross — you handled the diagonals and carry correctly!

exercises.questionText: For 21 × 32, Step 2 (cross, no carry from Step 1): 2×2 + 1×3 = ?

sessionFlow.coachHook: Step 3 is the left vertical — tens × tens, plus any carry from Step 2. This gives the leading digits.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Step 3 done — you have all three pieces of the answer!

sessionFlow.coachHook: Now put all three steps together to get the final answer in one sweep!
sessionFlow.boardDemo: 21×32: Step1=2, Step2=7, Step3=6. Answer: 672. 31×22: Step1=2, Step2=8, Step3=6. Answer: 682.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Full criss-cross complete — all three steps flowing perfectly!

sessionFlow.subtopic: MCQ: identify the middle step value
sessionFlow.coachHook: Quick quiz: I will show a multiplication — you tell me the middle (cross) step value before computing the full answer.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Perfect cross identification — you can now find the middle step at a glance!

sessionFlow.coachHook: Work through 32 × 24 one step at a time. Fill in each partial product as we build the final answer.
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: All three steps nailed — 768 is correct!
sessionFlow.instantFeedbackRetry: Step2=16, write 6 carry 1. Step3=3×2+1=7. Full answer: 768.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Now do 24 × 32 — should give the same answer!

sessionFlow.instantFeedbackWin: Speed criss-cross master! Five problems down in no time.
sessionFlow.reviewPrompt: Which step trips you up the most? Practise that step.

exercises.solution: 2×1=2. 4×1+2×2=8, no carry. 4×2=8. Wait — Step2: 4×1+2×2=8, no carry. Answer: 882.
